documents.content:
Interview synthesis — do small shops want delivery reminders by text?
8 people; top theme: tell me the window, not that it is coming (6 of 8)

## Themes
- "Tell me the window, not that it's coming" — 6 of 8: a reminder without a slot is noise; the window lets them plan the floor.
- "Text is fine, email gets lost" — 5 of 8: text reaches them on the floor; email is read at night.
- "Let me forward it to whoever is in" — 3 of 8: the person who ordered is often not the one receiving.

## Quotes
- Window: "A text saying 'tomorrow' is useless; tomorrow is twelve hours." (P2) — "Give me the two-hour slot and I will clear the back door." (P5)
- Text over email: "I do not open email until the shop is shut." (P1)
- Forwarding: "Half the time it is my Saturday girl who takes it in." (P4)

## Surprises
- The assumption was that reminders reduce missed deliveries; P6 never misses one and has nowhere to put an early one — one person's point.
- Nobody asked to turn reminders off; the worry was content, not volume.

## Open questions
- Whether the carrier gives a window for the common routes; no one could say.
